findings.where: Body, the 'Vibe' section heading (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: This one heading is styled exactly like a link: turquoise, italic and underlined. A tap or click on it does nothing, since it is static text. Its sibling heading 'Surf' is plain ink, so the two section titles also look like they do two different jobs. The turquoise is a fill colour used as text.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker, who taps 'Vibe' expecting a page about Canggu's social scene or a filter for party hostels, gets no response and wonders whether the page is broken. On a phone, which is where most of them read this, there is no hover to tell them otherwise.

findings.where: 'Good for' section, all twelve chips (First-time surfers through Sunsets), desktop and phone
findings.fault: The chips have their own box, a pill shape, a fill and a border, so they look like filter chips you can tap to narrow down hostels. All of them are static. On a hostel-search brand whose product is filtering by vibe and surf, a 'Budget' or 'Solo travellers' pill strongly suggests a filter.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who wants budget or solo-friendly hostels taps 'Budget', nothing happens, and they are left unsure whether the filter failed or the site is unfinished.

findings.fault: There are twelve chips in a rainbow of fills: yellow, mint, red-pink, lagoon, purple, hot pink. Each has a border in a different, clashing colour (a pink edge on yellow, a cyan edge on pink, a yellow edge on red). None of the colours means anything: 'Budget' and 'First-time surfers' share a colour for no reason. Purple and hot pink are not in the brand palette at all. The yellow and red-pink sit on amber (rewards only) and on coral and danger (actions and errors). The section is the loudest thing on the page and reads as a children's sticker sheet, not a calm guide.
findings.who_objects: The visitor reads the colours as categories and looks for a legend that isn't there. The founder would object because the brand's rule is one job per colour, and colour carrying no information is barred from the working area.

findings.where: The 'coming soon' notice at the foot of the content (desktop-02, phone-01)
findings.fault: The launch notice sits on a bright alarm-red panel, the colour of an error or a sold-out state, not on the ink ground the brand names for its interior announcement. The message is neutral to good news, but the panel shouts that something has gone wrong. On desktop the text fills only the left half of a full-width red slab, so the panel looks half-empty.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker scrolls down, hits a red box and reads it as an error before reading the words. The founder would object because red-for-error is a semantic colour, and the announcement block has a set night-ground treatment.

findings.where: Page title (h1) 'Best Hostels in Canggu' against the page's content
findings.fault: The title promises a ranked list of hostels, and the page holds none. The visitor only learns at the very bottom, in the notice, that listings are 'coming soon'. The title is also in Title Case, against the brand's sentence-case rule.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who arrives from a search for 'best hostels Canggu' expects names and prices. They scroll the whole page, find none, and leave feeling baited, which costs trust in a brand whose product is trust.

findings.where: Nav 'Destinations' and 'How we rank', the logo home link, and footer 'Privacy', 'Terms', 'How we rank', 'Report content'
findings.fault: Every link except the email address goes nowhere useful. Per the parts map, they lead back to this page or to a #destinations anchor that does not exist here. The page also ends with no next step: no other destination to explore and no way to hear when Canggu listings open.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker wants to see how hostels will be ranked, or to look at Uluwatu or Lombok instead. Every click returns them to the same page, so they hit a dead end and leave for Hostelworld.

findings.where: Section headings down the body: 'Surf', 'Vibe', 'Good for', 'WHAT TO LOOK FOR'
findings.fault: Four sibling sections use four different heading treatments: plain Quicksand, turquoise underlined italic, a larger Quicksand, and a small letter-spaced uppercase eyebrow. The last section looks like a label rather than a heading of equal rank, and uppercase is reserved for badges. The page's outline is hard to scan.
findings.who_objects: A visitor skimming on a phone for the practical part ('what should I look for in a hostel') can't tell which sections are peers. The useful advice looks like a footnote under the chips.

findings.where: Intro, 'Surf', 'Vibe', 'What to look for' and the notice paragraphs, desktop and phone
findings.fault: Body copy is fully justified, so word gaps stretch unevenly. This is worst on phone, in the notice ('MantaHostels   is   launching   across') and in the intro ('workers   and   long-stay').
findings.who_objects: Phone readers, the primary audience, stumble over the gappy lines. The text looks untidy for a brand selling craft.

findings.where: Top of page (first screen) and the desktop layout as a whole
findings.fault: There is no destination hero: no turquoise ground, illustration or image of Canggu, just a text column on sand. On desktop the column takes the left third, and the right two-thirds of the first screen are empty. Widths also disagree down the page: text at about 520 px, the chips running wider, and the notice at full width. Nothing aligns into one column.
findings.who_objects: A twenty-something choosing between Bali spots gets no sense of place, and the page feels like an unfinished draft, the 'sterile' look the brand names as its enemy. On desktop the empty half reads as a missing image or a broken layout.

findings.where: Intro and 'What to look for', the place names
findings.fault: The copy relies on local names (Berawa, Echo Beach, Batu Bolong, Old Man's) that a first-timer doesn't know. It gives no sense of where they are or how they differ, and no rough cost. Yet the advice is 'how close it is to Batu Bolong or Berawa'.
findings.who_objects: The first-time visitor to Bali can't act on 'stay near Batu Bolong or Berawa' without knowing which suits a surfer and which a partier. The deciding question the page exists for stays half-answered.
